text:
alex: quick sync — sketching a small RFC for a "credits-mapper" prototype that attributes prefetch/cache savings across routes/tenants and then surfaces that as a preview in the cost dashboard. want a fast gut-check before i file a PR. key questions: who owns the credit (requester vs origin route), session vs per-invocation split, and how to display fallbacks.

maria: :eyes: love the idea. UX needs a clear 'what-if' toggle: show cost with/without prefetch credits, and a tooltip that explains the allocation logic. also we should avoid surprise negative charges in invoice previews.

cheng: telemetry note — if we do heavy attribution we need to sample traces or we'll blow ingest. propose 5% sampling + deterministic hashing to keep per-tenant continuity. also watch for correlated spikes when we flip on credits (metrics bump).

sam: algorithm thought: attribute credits proportionally by observed token-share across candidate routes at time of prefetch, with a small stable floor for multipath cases. i.e. if route A consumed 70% of prefetched tokens in a session window, it gets 70% of credit. session_window should be configurable.

alex: sketch config prototype (very rough):
```json
{
  "mapper_v0": {
    "mode": "proportional",
    "session_window_s": 300,
    "min_credit_pct": 0.01,
    "sample_rate": 0.05
  }
}
```

maria: UX implications: we should surface both the allocated credit and the unapplied residue (small leftover tokens that can't be cleanly attributed). show both in the per-route breakdown and as a consolidated "prefetch credit" line in invoices.

cheng: for telemetry schema, we need: prefetch_id, origin_route, consumer_route, tokens_prefetched, tokens_consumed_window, attribution_pct, sample_flag. keep event size small (no prompt body).

alex: good call. also need to account for fallbacks: if a request falls back to a cheaper model variant after a cache miss, we shouldn't over-credit the origin. i suggest credits only applied when a prefetched KV hit occurs (i.e., consumer used cached KV).

sam: edge case: shared prefetched KV (multi-tenant caches on Dedicated) — we should avoid double-crediting tenants. possible approach: only allow credits on owner tenant but surface a "shared-savings" allocation to consumers for observability (not invoice).

maria: rollout UX: console should have a preview toggle (per-tenant) and a global admin preview. canary flow: enable credits-mapper=on for 10% of production tenants, show both raw and credited cost in the cost card. add a small banner: "estimates only — not on invoices" during canary.

ops-bot: deploy-bot: canary flag set scheduled for 2026-04-02 18:00 UTC to 10% ring. monitor metric: credited_cost_delta_p50 / credited_cost_delta_95.

cheng: sampling follow-up — store attribution samples keyed by (tenant, prefetch_id) so we can backfill estimates if we bump sample rate later. deterministically pick sampled tenants by hash(tenant_id) < sample_rate.

alex: next steps I propose: 1) i'll open a prototype PR with mapper_v0 and a sampling hook, 2) add lightweight telemetry event spec (cheng will draft), 3) maria will mock console preview (small card + what-if toggle), 4) sam will write a short test harness to simulate hotpath attribution. aim to have a canary-ready build in 2 weeks.

maria: :thumbsup: i'll add copy for the banner and the tooltip.

sam: i'll seed the harness with a couple of churny tenants — will share results in the PR.

alex: agreed. one ask: when we show the estimator in the console, annotate uncertainty (sampling, min_credit_pct) so PMs and billing know it's probabilistic during canary. ok to proceed?

maria: yes please proceed.

cheng: go ahead from infra side, just need schema + retention limits.

ops-bot: note: create incident channel if credited_cost_delta_95 > 20% for any customer during canary.

alex: thanks all — filing PR after lunch. will tag everyone. :coffee:
